mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar rate hikes, or the Sharpe ratio of SPX 20d returns vs. risk-free is not significantly lower than in pre-tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weaker labor market conditions encourage equity reallocation from labor-intensive sectors to capital-intensive ones.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.5% month-on-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such triggers are not statistically outperforming a baseline of 0% over 50 such events.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO by at least 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates robust demand, which precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with demand outpacing supply
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically positive in 80% of such demand-supply gaps.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% for two consecutive months signals supply contraction, which is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate profit-taking.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >=3% month-on-month for 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >50% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months during a non-recessionary regime, it predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower rates incentivize equity accumulation.
failure_condition: 60-day returns under this regime are not consistently outperforming a 0% baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by over 10% in a month is followed by a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market adjusts to weaker employment momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >10% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative in 80% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% each month for two months predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer confidence supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >1% month-on-month for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day returns under such triggers are not statistically positive in 75% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by 5% or more for two consecutive months, it indicates softening demand, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as equities adjust for slower growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >=5% month-on-month for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain non-negative in >50% of such events.
